summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 6 upside misses — VRT +17%, ORCL +11%, FLEX +10%, LH +9%, SNDK +7%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (FFIV -21%, CSGP -15%, CHRW -12%, LII -10%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: FFIV (-20.90%) — Not confirmed by search. The -20.9% gap is most likely the reaction to F5's fiscal Q4 earnings and FY27 guidance, which it usually reports in late October. No same-day article was found. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe: FFIV is a mid-cap networking/security software name that no strategy lists. If it was reported after the close, the gap happened overnight and the bot's pre-market signals had nothing to act on. A long-only bot also can't trade a -21% drop.

top_movers.catalyst: Q3 earnings beat: sales $4.31B (+61% y/y) vs ~$3.76B est, adj EPS $2.21 vs $1.82, organic orders +100%; FY26 guidance raised on AI data-center demand.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: VRT is a ~$90B mid/large-cap AI data-center power and cooling industrial that no strategy lists. The gap came from an earnings release before the open, which a post-open momentum or news-reactive signal can't front-run.
top_movers.suggestion: Add an AI-infrastructure/industrials bucket (VRT, ETN, GEV, etc.) to the momentum universe, plus an earnings-gap rule: enter names gapping ≥ +8% on ≥2× average volume within 30 minutes of the open.

top_movers.catalyst: Oracle's investor day laid out a funding plan: free cash flow positive in 2H FY2028 (~$30B in FY2029), extra equity and debt capped at $20B through FY2030. This eased financing worries and the stock rose about 10-11%.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. ORCL is a large-cap US tech name that no strategy's universe includes. The move was a scheduled-event gap and re-rating, so a technical or momentum filter would not have caught it even if the stock had been in the universe.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap US tech (ORCL and similar AI-infrastructure names) to the news-reactive strategy's universe. Also add an event-gate rule that admits names with a gap of +8% or more on 2x or more average volume after an investor-day or guidance catalyst.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed same-day news. Flex reported fiscal Q2 2027 results on Oct 28 (before the open), so the +9.7% move is likely a lagged earnings and AI-datacenter re-rating. I couldn't find the results or the Oct 29 reaction.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: FLEX is a mid-cap EMS/electronics manufacturer (Nasdaq, Singapore-domiciled), not in any strategy's list. Any post-earnings gap would also have been filtered or already priced by the open.
top_movers.suggestion: Add FLEX and similar AI-supply-chain EMS names (JBL, CLS, SANM) to the momentum universe. Also let the earnings-gate release names 1 day after results if close-to-close return ≥ +5% on volume ≥ 1.5× the 20-day average.

top_movers.catalyst: Likely Q3 2026 earnings reaction (results due pre-market Oct 28–29; consensus EPS ~$4.64, rev ~$3.76B). I couldn't find the actual figures, so the beat/raise is inferred, not confirmed.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: LH is a large-cap healthcare diagnostics name that no strategy covers. Even if it were in a universe, an earnings gap-up would likely trip the earnings gate or gap filters before the post-results signal.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap healthcare/diagnostics (LH, DGX) to the news-reactive universe. Let the earnings-gate release names with a post-results gap ≥ +5% on ≥1.5× average volume within 30 minutes of the open.

top_movers.catalyst: No SNDK-specific news found for 10/29; likely a memory/NAND sector rally on AI storage demand (Micron/WDC strength) extending the late-October run, with the stock near $1,400.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: SNDK is a recent-spinoff, ~$1,400/share mid/large-cap memory name that no strategy includes. Its price and extreme volatility likely also fail price-cap or volatility screens.
top_movers.suggestion: Add SNDK, and peers MU and WDC, to the momentum-trader universe, with position sizing by ATR or a dollar-notional cap so the ~$1,400 share price doesn't break the per-share price filter.

top_movers.catalyst: Q3 2026 results reported Oct 28: revenue $5.5B (+7.2%, organic +6.2%), adj. EPS $1.34 (+25%) vs ~$1.21 consensus, book-to-bill 1.03, and full-year guidance raised.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: GEHC is a large-cap medical-device name that no strategy lists. It was also an earnings gap-up, where positioning happens before the print and post-gap momentum or RSI filters would likely have excluded it.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap healthcare/medtech names like GEHC to the momentum universe, and let the earnings gate release names with a post-earnings gap ≥ +5% on a beat-and-raise, entering at the open of day 2 (day-1 close was +6.49%).

top_movers.catalyst: Not confirmed by search. The -20.9% gap is most likely the reaction to F5's fiscal Q4 earnings and FY27 guidance, which it usually reports in late October. No same-day article was found.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: FFIV is a mid-cap networking/security software name that no strategy lists. If it was reported after the close, the gap happened overnight and the bot's pre-market signals had nothing to act on. A long-only bot also can't trade a -21% drop.
top_movers.suggestion: Add FFIV-type mid-cap tech names to the news-reactive universe, and add a post-earnings gap-down screen (gap ≤ -15% on ≥3× avg volume) that flags names for a watchlist or mean-reversion entry after day-2 stabilization. A long-only bot can't short the drop.

top_movers.catalyst: Likely post-Q3 2026 earnings selloff (report due ~Oct 28–29; options implied about ±15%). I couldn't find coverage of the actual results. Prior quarters showed weak guidance and Homes.com/bookings concerns.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: CSGP is a mid-cap, already-crushed (~-50–70% YTD) real-estate data/internet name. The move was an earnings gap, so a long-only momentum or mean-reversion bot had no entry signal, and shorting isn't possible.
top_movers.suggestion: Add an earnings-gap watchlist rule: include mid-caps with options-implied earnings moves ≥10% in the news-reactive universe, and flag gaps ≤-10% on ≥3× volume for a next-day mean-reversion check.

top_movers.catalyst: Likely Q3 2026 earnings reaction (CHRW reported around Oct 28-29) amid weak freight demand and margin worries. Searches found no same-day coverage, so this is unconfirmed.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: CHRW is a mid-cap freight/logistics name that no strategy includes. An earnings-day gap of about -12% would also have been caught by gap and earnings gates, and the bot is long-only with no short capability.
top_movers.suggestion: Add mid-cap transports/logistics (CHRW, EXPD, JBHT) to the news-reactive universe, and let the earnings-gate release names with a post-results gap of 8% or more once the first 30 minutes of volume confirm. A long-only bot would still gain nothing on a decline, so this is only a watchlist/rebound signal.

top_movers.catalyst: Q3 results on Oct 28: adj. EPS $6.84 (-7% y/y), Home Comfort margin down 490bp on competition, inflation and dealer destocking. FY guidance was reportedly cut. The stock fell about 10% the next day.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: LII is a mid-cap HVAC industrial that no strategy covers. The gap came from an after-close earnings release, so a pre-market momentum or news filter had no entry before the drop. The bot also appears to be long-only.
top_movers.suggestion: Add mid-cap industrials (S&P 400, market cap above $10B) to the universe. Also add a post-earnings-gap rule that flags names gapping down 8% or more on 2x average volume, for watchlist or mean-reversion review. Shorting is out of scope.
